From d5028f9f7d8de5c375c52b98976b6f310e73398f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Vladimir Davydov <vdavydov@parallels.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2015 14:59:20 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] vmscan: fix sane_reclaim helper for legacy memcg

The sane_reclaim() helper is supposed to return false for memcg reclaim
if the legacy hierarchy is used, because the latter lacks dirty
throttling mechanism, and so it did before it was accidentally broken by
commit 33398cf2f360c ("memcg: export struct mem_cgroup").  Fix it.

Fixes: 33398cf2f360c ("memcg: export struct mem_cgroup")
Signed-off-by: Vladimir Davydov <vdavydov@parallels.com>
Acked-by: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>
Acked-by: Michal Hocko <mhocko@suse.com>
Cc: Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/mm/vmscan.c b/mm/vmscan.c
index 2d978b28a410..7f63a9381f71 100644
--- a/mm/vmscan.c
+++ b/mm/vmscan.c
@@ -175,7 +175,7 @@ static bool sane_reclaim(struct scan_control *sc)
 	if (!memcg)
 		return true;
 #ifdef CONFIG_CGROUP_WRITEBACK
-	if (memcg->css.cgroup)
+	if (cgroup_on_dfl(memcg->css.cgroup))
 		return true;
 #endif
 	return false;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `mm/vmscan.c`**
- The condition in the `sane_reclaim` function was modified. 
- The original line `if (memcg->css.cgroup)` was changed to `if (cgroup_on_dfl(memcg->css.cgroup))`. 
- This change ensures that the function correctly identifies when the legacy memory cgroup hierarchy is in use, returning false for reclaim operations in that case.

### Relationships
- The patch addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit (identified as `33398cf2f360c`), which altered the behavior of the `sane_reclaim` function. 
- The modification restores the intended functionality of the helper, ensuring it behaves correctly for legacy memory cgroup hierarchies that do not support dirty throttling. 
- The change is part of a broader effort to maintain the integrity of memory management in the kernel, particularly in relation to control groups (cgroups).

```
Reason:
The condition checks if the memory cgroup (`memcg`) has an associated cgroup. If it does, the function incorrectly returns true, allowing reclaim operations for legacy memory cgroup hierarchies, which should not be allowed due to the absence of a dirty throttling mechanism.

The code statements that fix the bug are:

if (cgroup_on_dfl(memcg->css.cgroup))
```
```c
return true;
```
Reason:
The fix changes the condition to check if the memory cgroup is on the default hierarchy (`cgroup_on_dfl`). This ensures that reclaim operations return true only for memory cgroups that are part of the default hierarchy, thereby correctly returning false for legacy memory cgroup hierarchies and preventing incorrect reclaim operations.
